'Bar chart of revenue by genre, weighted to avoid double-counting multi-genre films. Action leads with $90.8 billion, followed by Comedy at $85.7 billion and Adventure at $78.9 billion. Includes a play control to animate the chart by release year.'
'''Segoe UI Bold'', wf_segoe-ui_bold, helvetica, arial, sans-serif'
'Hidden Gems: 2.4 percent of eligible films, 246 out of 10,259, meet the hidden gem criteria.'
'''Segoe UI Bold'', wf_segoe-ui_bold, helvetica, arial, sans-serif'

'Table of the top 6 studios by revenue, including average budget, movie count, strategy classification, and ROI. Universal Pictures leads with $26.4 billion in revenue across 630 films. Marvel Studios has the highest ROI at 3.5 times despite only 37 films and the highest average budget at $186.4 million.'

'Side-by-side keyword comparison. All-movie keywords are led by "based on novel or book" at 9.6 percent share. Blockbuster keywords are led by "sequel" at 38 percent, showing little overlap between the two groups'' most common terms. Adjustable slider sets how many top keywords are shown.'

'Two donut charts showing revenue concentration under the Pareto view. Left: the smallest group of films reaching 80 percent of total revenue represents $525 billion, or 80 percent of revenue, from films worth $131 billion individually below that threshold. Right: just 1.9 thousand films, 18.2 percent of the total, drive 80 percent of all revenue. Includes a Pareto and Top N toggle to switch views.'

'Scatter plot of budget versus total revenue, with a positive trend line. Correlation is 0.73, R-squared is 54.0 percent, meaning budget explains just over half of the variation in revenue. Includes a 5-step dimension selector and a highlight toggle for blockbuster films.'
